newsitem.title: LEBANON: Court, ministry in row over Lebanese election.
newsitem.headline: Court, ministry in row over Lebanese election.

text.p: A judge of Lebanon's Constitutional Council accused the Interior Ministry on Friday of negligence in failing to supply evidence it needs to rule on appeals against the results of last month's parliamentary election.
Interior Minister Michel al-Murr, whose ministry organised the elections widely criticised for alleged fraud, intimidation and vote-buying, responded that the court was trying to order him around.

"Neither the interior minister nor the ministry is employed by the Constitutional Council," Murr was quoted by Lebanon's National News Agency as saying. However, he promised to deliver the requested evidence.
The public clash between the ministry and the court, formed last year as the first independent body with the right to rule on election disputes, is unprecedented.
Government supporters won all but a handful of the 128 parliamentary seats and the court has received 17 appeals by defeated candidates to overturn results on grounds of fraud.
Mohammed Majzoub, a member of the 10-man court, said the ministry was guilty of "negligence and tardiness" in failing to deliver the evidence despite two requests since September 26.

He and another judge accused the ministry of disrespectful and unconstitutional behaviour towards the court, which can cancel the election of individual deputies and award their seats to other candidates if it decides serious fraud existed.
The court has asked the ministry for voting reports, candidates' personal files and voter lists it needs as evidence but has received no response, Majzoub said.
"This is our first experience in having a Constitutional Council, and we do not like the way they (the ministry) are dealing with us," Majzoub told Reuters in an interview.
"It seems they are not acquainted with the idea of cancelling someone's parliamentary representation," he added.

Another member of the court, who asked not to be identified, said: "We have received no positive response from the Interior Ministry, on the contrary we have received disrespectful behaviour towards the council.
"We are afraid that some of the necessary documents have been destroyed," he added.
News of the confrontation broke on Thursday when the court took the unprecedented step of having its latest ruling demanding the evidence published in a Beirut newspaper.
"The delay by the Interior Ministry...is leading to the existence of an unconstitutional situation for which the ministry will be responsible," the court said.
